title: Bitcoin Internals
subtitle: A Technical Guide to Bitcoin
gist: A short technical guide to Bitcoin's workings: how the blockchain tracks ownership and prevents double-spending, the cryptography behind transactions, and how proof-of-work mining creates coins. For technically minded readers.

title: On the Origins of Bitcoin
subtitle: Stages of Monetary Evolution
free_link_note: Free PDF from author's site (monograph-length work)
sources: Author blog post links PDF (200, application/pdf)
gist: An economic and historical study of Bitcoin's origin and value as money, relating it to Austrian economics, Mises's regression theorem and Menger's evolutionary account of money. For readers interested in monetary theory.

title: Bitcoin
subtitle: And the Future of Money
notes: Triumph Books, Sept 2014. ISBN 9781629370361. Covers the dark side incl. FBI interviews.
gist: A CNNMoney reporter's introduction to Bitcoin: its origins, how it works and is used today, its economic implications and its illicit uses, with interviews from regulators to advocates. For general readers.

title: Bitcoin for the Befuddled
notes: No Starch Press, 2014.
gist: A plain-language, illustrated introduction to Bitcoin that explains how it works, how to acquire and use it, and how to mine it. For complete beginners.

title: Bitcoin: a moeda na era digital
notes: Mises Brasil, 2014, preface by Jeffrey Tucker. Austrian-economics framing. A free PDF from Mises Brasil may exist but was not verified.
sources: Instituto Ludwig von Mises Brasil (ISBN 9788581190761); Mises journal review
gist: A Portuguese-language introduction to Bitcoin that explains its origins and how it works, then analyzes it through Austrian School economics and monetary freedom. Aimed at general readers.

title: Bitcoin: The Future of Money?
notes: Published by Unbound (crowdfunded). Early mainstream look at Bitcoin and the Satoshi identity question.
gist: Tells the story of Bitcoin from Satoshi Nakamoto's appearance after the 2008 crisis, explaining in plain language how it works and what it could mean for the state. For general readers.

title: God Is a Gamer
notes: Indian financial thriller with Bitcoin central to the plot; often called the first Bitcoin thriller.
gist: A thriller novel in which a struggling gaming company, a banker's suspicious death and a US terror investigation are tied together through Bitcoin and the dark web. Fiction for general readers.

title: The Anatomy of a Money-Like Informational Commodity
subtitle: A Study of Bitcoin
free_link_note: Free PDF released by the author on his own site (no explicit license, offered as 'available for free'). Not on GitHub.
evidence: The author's blog ofnumbers.com/the-anatomy/ and his 2014 announcement post both say the book is 'all available for free in PDF and Scribd formats'. The PDF link on that page returns HTTP 200, application/pdf, 6.8 MB. The older S3 link from the announcement is dead (404).
gist: A free, book-length study of Bitcoin that treats it as an informational commodity, covering public goods, mining, deflation, network effects and legal issues. For readers wanting an analytical view.

title: The Bitcoin Big Bang
subtitle: How Alternative Currencies Are About to Change the World
notes: Wiley, 2014. CNBC contributor.
gist: A currency trader's guide that goes beyond Bitcoin basics, placing digital currency in the history of payments and examining how it may affect business and the future of money. For general and business readers.

title: The Book of Satoshi
subtitle: The Collected Writings of Bitcoin Creator Satoshi Nakamoto
notes: e53 Publishing. Spanish translation 'El Libro de Satoshi'.
gist: Compiles Satoshi Nakamoto's emails, forum posts and the Bitcoin white paper in chronological order, with explanations of Bitcoin fundamentals and its economic implications.

title: Understanding Bitcoin
subtitle: Cryptography, Engineering and Economics
gist: A technical guide to the cryptography, engineering and economics of Bitcoin, from public key cryptography through transactions, the blockchain and mining, plus competing economic views. Aimed at finance professionals.

title: 暗号が通貨になる「ビットコイン」のからくり
subtitle: 数式なしでわかる仮想通貨の技術
notes: Kodansha Blue Backs, May 2014. Romanized: Angō ga tsūka ni naru 'Bitcoin' no karakuri. Authors: Yoshimoto Yoshio, Nishida Munechika.
sources: Kodansha Blue Backs; NIMS library catalogue (ISBN 9784062578660)
Agora web article by the author
lopp.net bitcoin books pages; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: A Japanese Blue Backs book explaining the mathematics and cryptography behind Bitcoin and its economic impact, comparing it with government-backed currency and electronic money. For general readers.

title: Are Bitcoins Ownable?
subtitle: Property Rights, IP Wrongs, and Legal Theory Implications
free_link_note: Free PDF from author's site (also sold as ebook/print)
gist: A monograph asking whether bitcoins can be owned as property, using an action-based theory of property rights and noting that Bitcoin fits poorly into existing legal categories. For readers in law and libertarian theory.

title: Bit by Bit
subtitle: How P2P Is Freeing the World
gist: Argues that peer-to-peer technology, with Bitcoin as a prime example, is reshaping social, economic and political life by letting people cooperate without central control.

title: Bitcoin Basics
gist: A short question-and-answer guide with 101 entries for beginners, covering Bitcoin's origins, who runs the network, mining, security, value, and common objections.

title: Bitcoin – Geld ohne Staat
notes: FinanzBuch Verlag 2015, 208 pp. Austrian-school perspective.
gist: A German-language introduction to Bitcoin that views it through Austrian-school economics as free-market money, explains the blockchain, and includes interviews with Bitcoin figures such as Roger Ver and Gavin Andresen.

title: Digital Gold
subtitle: Bitcoin and the Inside Story of the Misfits and Millionaires Trying to Reinvent Money
notes: Harper, 2015. German translation exists.
gist: A journalist's narrative history of Bitcoin and the people behind it, from early cypherpunk experiments through the Mt. Gox era and the rise of Bitcoin startups.

title: The Age of Cryptocurrency
subtitle: How Bitcoin and Digital Money Are Challenging the Global Economic Order
notes: Mostly Bitcoin-focused despite the generic title. UK edition titled 'Cryptocurrency: How Bitcoin and Digital Money Are Challenging the Global Economic Order'.
gist: Explains Bitcoin and the cryptocurrency idea, how digital money works and why it matters, with attention to its potential to change finance. For general readers.

title: Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies
subtitle: A Comprehensive Introduction
free_link_note: Free PDF (final draft) linked from the official Princeton book site
notes: The 'Princeton textbook'; accompanies the Coursera course. Largely Bitcoin, with a chapter on altcoins.
gist: A textbook-style introduction to how Bitcoin works, covering cryptography, mining, anonymity and altcoins. For students, developers and researchers.

title: Bitcoin For Dummies
notes: Wiley, 2016. 'Prypto' = Peter Kent & Tyler Bain.
gist: A beginner's guide to understanding the Bitcoin market, setting up a wallet, buying, storing and using bitcoin, and protecting against fraud and theft.

title: The Internet of Money
subtitle: A collection of talks by Andreas M. Antonopoulos
free_link_note: CC-BY-NC-ND (book text in /chapters), full manuscript in AsciiDoc; build system MIT. Repo is a re-upload of the original MerkleBloom source, not hosted under the author's own account.
notes: Volume 1 (2016), Volume 2 (2017), Volume 3 (2019); edited talk transcripts. Spanish translation 'Internet del Dinero'.
evidence: Every commit (initial commit, README, 'second print edition', Jan 2017) is authored by Andreas M. Antonopoulos <andreas@antonopoulos.com>. The README says the source is for the book published by MerkleBloom LLC and that the chapters are licensed CC-BY-NC-ND, and the LICENSE says 'Copyright (c) 2017 merklebloom'. The author granted the license, so verbatim non-commercial redistribution is allowed. The github.com/merklebloom org now only has bookbuilder and docker-asciidoctor, so the original repo seems to have been removed. Consider linking with that caveat.
gist: A collection of Andreas Antonopoulos's talks and essays on why Bitcoin matters, covering its philosophical, social and historical implications rather than how it works technically.

title: The Politics of Bitcoin
subtitle: Software as Right-Wing Extremism
sources: Goodreads list 'Bitcoin Books'; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: A short critical book arguing that Bitcoin's supporters hold a cyberlibertarian outlook that leans on far-right political thought, tracing its ideas from Friedman, Hayek and Mises to Fed conspiracy theories.

title: American Kingpin
subtitle: The Epic Hunt for the Criminal Mastermind Behind the Silk Road
notes: Silk Road / Ross Ulbricht. Bitcoin is the market's currency and plays a major role, but the book is a crime story rather than about Bitcoin itself.
gist: The story of Ross Ulbricht and the Silk Road, the dark web marketplace that ran on Bitcoin, and the investigation that brought it down. A narrative true-crime account.

title: Attack of the 50 Foot Blockchain
subtitle: Bitcoin, Blockchain, Ethereum & Smart Contracts
gist: A sceptical, non-technical tour of Bitcoin, blockchain, Ethereum and smart contracts up to mid-2017, covering energy use, exchange hacks, Mt. Gox, Silk Road and mining concentration.

title: Bitcoin, la monnaie acéphale
notes: CNRS Éditions, 2017.
gist: A French-language book on Bitcoin as a leaderless, headless money, taking a deliberately contrarian view of established economic ideas. Co-written by a historian-banker and a digital specialist.

title: How Money Got Free
subtitle: Bitcoin and the Fight for the Future of Finance
gist: An account of Bitcoin's rise from fringe idea to financial industry attention, following the people and companies building around it. For general readers.

title: Pay the Devil in Bitcoin
subtitle: The Collapse of Mt. Gox
notes: Kindle Single, Sept 2017; written with Mark Karpelès's cooperation. Subtitle varies by listing. Expanded into 'The Devil Takes Bitcoin' (2025).
gist: A nonfiction account of the collapse of Mt. Gox, the Tokyo bitcoin exchange that lost nearly half a billion dollars of bitcoin, written with input from its owner Mark Karpeles and former staff.

title: The Internet of Money, Volume Two
gist: A second collection of eleven Andreas Antonopoulos talks, including 'Blockchain vs Bullshit' and 'Currency Wars', with a new FAQ section. It can be read without Volume One.

title: Bitcoin and Beyond
subtitle: Cryptocurrencies, Blockchains, and Global Governance
free_link_note: Open Access, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Routledge RIPE series); also PDF on OAPEN (library.oapen.org handle 20.500.12657/29557). Academic edited volume; partly covers blockchain beyond Bitcoin
sources: DOI resolves (200) to Taylor & Francis OA page; license per OAPEN metadata via search (OAPEN blocked automated fetch)
notes: Academic open-access volume that also covers blockchains beyond Bitcoin.
gist: An academic edited volume by scholars from several disciplines on what Bitcoin and blockchains mean for global governance, with chapters on anti-money-laundering rules and The DAO.

title: Bitcoin – Métamorphoses
subtitle: De l'or des fous à l'or numérique ?
notes: Dunod, 2018. Follow-up to 'La monnaie acéphale'.
gist: A French-language book that surveys Bitcoin's history, its antifragility, criticisms, the 'blockchain bullshit' trend and smart contracts, and challenges media coverage. A follow-up to La monnaie acephale.

title: The Bitcoin Standard
subtitle: The Decentralized Alternative to Central Banking
gist: Traces the history of money from shells and gold to central banking, then argues Bitcoin is a sound-money alternative to government currencies. For general readers.

title: Tutto su Bitcoin
notes: Hoepli, 2018. Practical guide; partly covers other cryptocurrencies.
gist: An Italian practical guide to investing in cryptocurrencies, explaining how to open exchange accounts and set up wallets, with a section on Ethereum, Litecoin, Dash and Monero.

title: 21 Lessons
subtitle: What I've Learned from Falling Down the Bitcoin Rabbit Hole
free_link_note: CC-BY-SA 4.0, read online on author's site; many translations at 21lessons.com/translations
gist: A personal, non-technical set of 21 lessons from the author's study of Bitcoin, in three sections covering philosophy, economics and technology.

title: Bitcoin & Black America
gist: Explores how Bitcoin and blockchain could help Black Americans build wealth, with a critique of the banking system, advice on using Bitcoin in work and business, and a list of Black blockchain professionals.

title: Bitcoin and Lightning Network on Raspberry Pi
subtitle: Running Nodes on Pi3, Pi4 and Pi Zero
free_link_note: Only companion source code from the publisher (Apress), not the book text.
notes: Apress, Nov 2019. Covers bitcoind, LND and c-lightning.
evidence: Official Apress org repo, description 'Source Code for ... by Harris Brakmic', homepage apress.com/us/book/9781484255216.
gist: A hands-on guide to running Bitcoin full nodes and Lightning nodes (LND and c-lightning) on Raspberry Pi, covering Bitcoin basics, mining and wallets via RPC. For makers comfortable with Linux.

title: Bitcoin Billionaires
subtitle: A True Story of Genius, Betrayal, and Redemption
notes: The Winklevoss twins' Bitcoin story.
gist: The story of Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss after the Facebook dispute, and their bet on Bitcoin and role in its early crypto industry. A narrative account.

title: Bitcoin Money
subtitle: A Tale of Bitville Discovering Good Money
notes: Illustrated by Marina Yakubivska. Spanish translation 'El Dinero Bitcoin: el cuento de Bitvilla'.
gist: A children's picture book about the town of Bitville, whose kids move from barter to fiat money and inflation until a newcomer named Satoshi introduces Bitcoin.

title: Grokking Bitcoin
free_link_note: Open-source version, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; free HTML on author's site, source at github.com/kallerosenbaum/grokkingbitcoin
sources: Author site rosenbaum.se/book (200) and repo LICENSE file. Note: grokkingbitcoin.com is now an unrelated book by another author
Manning; London Bitcoin Devs meetup listing
notes: Manning, 2019. Foreword by David A. Harding.
gist: A guide to how Bitcoin works, from hash functions and signatures through addresses, wallets, transactions, proof of work and the network, up to SegWit. Programming is not required.

title: Inventing Bitcoin
subtitle: The Technology Behind the First Truly Scarce and Decentralized Money Explained
free_link_note: Free ebook/audiobook copy offered by Swan (author's company) via 'Get your FREE copy' sign-up; delivery format not verified
sources: swanbitcoin.com/freebook redirects here (200); author is Swan co-founder
gist: A short primer on how Bitcoin works, covering transactions, blocks, proof-of-work mining, wallets, keys and scripting, using only high-school math.

title: Programming Bitcoin
subtitle: Learn How to Program Bitcoin from Scratch
free_link_note: CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0, full text (AsciiDoc chapters) and code on author's GitHub
notes: O'Reilly, 2019. Python implementation of Bitcoin primitives.
gist: A hands-on book for Python developers that teaches Bitcoin by building a library from scratch, covering elliptic curve math, transactions, Script, blocks, proof of work and networking.

title: The Internet of Money, Volume Three
gist: A third collection of twelve Andreas Antonopoulos talks about money as a tool of control and surveillance, financial inclusion, and what money could look like without a central authority.

title: The Little Bitcoin Book
subtitle: Why Bitcoin Matters for Your Freedom, Finances, and Future
gist: A short introduction by eight authors from five continents explaining what is wrong with today's money and how Bitcoin offers an alternative, with a 30-page FAQ. For readers with no technical or financial background.

title: Why Buy Bitcoin
subtitle: Investing Today in the Money of Tomorrow
gist: A wealth manager's investment case for Bitcoin, starting with the history of money, then covering its decentralized design and fixed supply, objections like volatility and energy, and comparisons with gold, stocks and real estate.

title: #SmartCustody
subtitle: The Use of Advanced Cryptographic Tools to Improve the Care, Maintenance, Control, and Protection of Digital Assets
free_link_note: CC-BY-SA 4.0, manuscript on GitHub
gist: A free guide to protecting digital assets that builds a risk-modeling method around a 14-step cold-storage self-custody scenario and 27 adversaries, for individual holders and family funds.

title: Bitcoin Clarity
subtitle: The Complete Beginners Guide to Understanding
gist: A self-published guide for non-technical readers that explains Bitcoin through conceptual mental models rather than code, written by a Blockstream sysadmin.

title: Bitcoin Red Pill
subtitle: O Renascimento Moral, Material e Tecnológico
notes: Brazilian. 3rd edition retitled '...O Renascimento Moral e Tecnológico'.
gist: A Portuguese-language introductory book presenting Bitcoin as a way to separate money from government, covering seigniorage, bailouts and fiat currency, with practical steps for using it.

title: Bitcoin, Blockchain, and Cryptoassets
subtitle: A Comprehensive Introduction
free_link_note: Companion University of Basel lecture slides (LaTeX), licensed CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0. These are not the book text.
notes: MIT Press 2020; translation of the German 'Bitcoin, Blockchain und Kryptoassets' (2017). Bitcoin is the core, but later chapters cover Ethereum/tokens.
evidence: Owned by cifunibas, the Center for Innovative Finance at the University of Basel (cif.unibas.ch), which is the authors' institute. The book comes out of this lecture. The repo holds slide .tex files only.
gist: A university textbook introducing Bitcoin, blockchain and cryptoassets, from monetary economics and the Bitcoin protocol to proof-of-work, game theory, volatility and regulation. Written for students and practitioners.

title: Bitcoin: Hard Money You Can't F*ck With
gist: A plain-language case that Bitcoin could become the next global reserve currency, covering why it matters now and a short history of money. Aimed at newcomers and conventional investors.

title: Cryptoeconomics
subtitle: Fundamental Principles of Bitcoin
free_link_note: Full text free on the libbitcoin GitHub wiki (print edition sold separately)
gist: Applies economic principles to Bitcoin to examine its design and common misunderstandings of it. Dense and conceptual rather than a how-to guide, so aimed at readers who already know Bitcoin.

title: Kings of Crypto
subtitle: One Startup's Quest to Take Cryptocurrency Out of Silicon Valley and Onto Wall Street
notes: History of Coinbase; Bitcoin-heavy early chapters but covers the broader crypto industry.
gist: A narrative account of Coinbase and its founder Brian Armstrong, following the company from startup to major cryptocurrency exchange. Suited to general readers interested in crypto business history.

title: Learning Bitcoin from the Command Line
free_link_note: CC-BY 4.0, read on GitHub (v2.2.2; v3.0 in progress); Spanish and Portuguese translations
sources: Official Blockchain Commons repo README (license section)
gist: A free tutorial teaching Bitcoin and Lightning by working directly with Bitcoin Core's command-line tools, covering wallets, transactions, Script and timelocks. Aimed at technical readers.

title: Magic Internet Money
subtitle: A Book About Bitcoin
gist: A plain-language introduction to Bitcoin by a Canadian finance professional, covering banking, cryptography, economics and governance and questioning common assumptions about money. For general readers.

title: Thank God for Bitcoin
subtitle: The Creation, Corruption and Redemption of Money
gist: A multi-author book that began as a Bible study, examining the morality of money, the flaws of the fiat system and how Bitcoin's principles align with Christian teaching. Written for Christian readers curious about Bitcoin.

title: The Price of Tomorrow
subtitle: Why Deflation Is the Key to an Abundant Future
gist: Argues that technology is inherently deflationary, which strains an economy built on debt and growth, and that societies must adapt. Covers automation, work and monetary policy; Bitcoin figures in the proposed answer. For general readers.

title: This Book Will Save You Time
gist: A short book on time as the scarce resource, drawing on personal finance and Austrian economics to question the 9-to-5 model; the author is a Bitcoin writer. Bitcoin's role in the book is unconfirmed.

title: Truth Decay
subtitle: How Bitcoin Fixes This
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: A book arguing that fiat money erodes trust and truth and that Bitcoin offers a fix, introducing what Bitcoin is, how it works and how to use it. Aimed at newcomers.

title: Bitcoin and the American Dream
gist: A short book written for US policymakers arguing that Bitcoin fits American values and is used by workers, minorities and veterans, not only technologists. Funded via Kickstarter.

title: Bitcoin Saves the World
notes: Self-published illustrated book for ages 6-12.

title: La filosofía de Bitcoin
subtitle: La caída del Estado
notes: Crowdfunded first edition (Dec 2021 per CriptoNoticias; some sources say 2022); Deusto (Planeta) edition Jan 2024. English translation 'The Philosophy of Bitcoin' (Bitcoin Magazine Books, 2023).
gist: A Spanish-language book arguing that Bitcoin redefines private property and that states lose sovereignty over it, likening Bitcoin to gunpowder, the printing press and the internet. Written in Spanish.

title: Layered Money
subtitle: From Gold and Dollars to Bitcoin and Central Bank Digital Currencies
gist: Traces money as layers built on a base asset such as gold, from Renaissance Florence through central banking to Bitcoin and CBDCs. Written for general readers, with no finance background required.

title: Mastering the Lightning Network
subtitle: A Second Layer Blockchain Protocol for Instant Bitcoin Payments
free_link_note: CC-BY-SA 4.0, read on GitHub
sources: Official repo github.com/lnbook/lnbook (GitHub API license CC-BY-SA-4.0)
notes: O'Reilly, Dec 2021.
gist: A practical guide to the Lightning Network, a second-layer payment protocol for Bitcoin, covering channels, routing, node operation, wire protocol, security and privacy. Aimed at intermediate to advanced readers and developers.

title: The 7th Property
subtitle: Bitcoin and the Monetary Revolution
gist: Argues that immutability is a seventh property of money and that central banking is a major moral hazard, examining the Federal Reserve closely before explaining how Bitcoin works. For readers new to Bitcoin.

title: The Bitcoin Shortcut
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)

title: The Blocksize War
subtitle: The battle over who controls Bitcoin's protocol rules
notes: Self-published 2021.
gist: A chronology of the 2015-2017 dispute over Bitcoin's block size, covering the big-block and small-block camps, SegWit2x and the creation of Bitcoin Cash, and who controls protocol rules. For readers wanting Bitcoin's governance history.

title: The Bullish Case for Bitcoin
gist: An expanded version of Boyapati's essay explaining how money emerges and why he considers Bitcoin superior to gold and fiat as sound money. A short, beginner-friendly read.

title: The Fiat Standard
subtitle: The Debt Slavery Alternative to Human Civilization
gist: Explains the modern fiat monetary system as a feat of engineering, covering the shift from the gold standard to government-backed money, as a companion to The Bitcoin Standard. For readers interested in monetary economics.

title: The Promise of Bitcoin
subtitle: The Future of Money and How It Can Work for You
gist: An introduction arguing Bitcoin is a more rational monetary system than traditional money, covering adoption, buying and investing strategies, and mining. Written by an early crypto entrepreneur for general readers.

title: Bitcoin & Exponential Freedom
subtitle: How Hard Money Restores Freedom & Prosperity
sources: Goodreads list 'Bitcoin, Money & the Economy'; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: Explains money, inflation and central banking from first principles and argues that Bitcoin is a structural improvement on earlier money. Written in plain English for general readers.

title: Bitcoin Development Philosophy
subtitle: A Guide for Bitcoin Developers
free_link_note: CC BY 4.0 (Chaincode Labs), free online; source github.com/bitcoin-dev-philosophy/btcphilosophy
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; Konsensus Network catalog (via litres.ru author page / konsensus.net search)
notes: Online edition circa 2022; print/ebook by Konsensus Network. Year not confirmed, left null.
gist: A guide to the design trade-offs behind Bitcoin, covering decentralization, trustlessness, privacy, finite supply and scaling, with links to further reading. Aimed at developers who already know Bitcoin basics.

title: Bitcoin Evangelism
sources: thingelstad.com Bitcoin Books list; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: A guide for helping everyday people understand Bitcoin and blockchain, covering sound money, inflation and common objections such as environmental criticism. Aimed at newcomers and those explaining Bitcoin to others.

title: Bitcoin Is Venice
gist: Essays arguing from critiques of modern economics and fiat money toward what a Bitcoin-standard economy and a possible new Renaissance might look like, drawing on Venice, Greece and Islamic finance. For readers with some Bitcoin background.

title: Bitcoin: Everything Divided by 21 Million
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; Konsensus Network catalog (via litres.ru author page / konsensus.net search)
Bitcoin Infinity Store; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: Explores how people relate to time, money and value and argues Bitcoin answers the problems of fiat money. Written by the creator of the infinity-divided-by-21-million meme for readers already curious about Bitcoin.

title: Check Your Financial Privilege
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; Bitcoin Magazine Books catalog (bitcoinmagazine.com/bitcoin-magazine-books)
gist: A collection of essays arguing that people born into reserve currencies hold an advantage over most of the world, with Bitcoin case studies from places such as Cuba, Sudan, Afghanistan and Nigeria. For general readers.

title: Do Bitcoin
gist: A short beginner's introduction to Bitcoin from first principles, covering why it was created and answering questions about altcoins, NFTs, miners and nodes. Aimed at complete newcomers.

title: The Simplest Bitcoin Book Ever Written
Tracers in the Dark
subtitle: The Global Hunt for the Crime Lords of Cryptocurrency
notes: Centres on Bitcoin blockchain tracing (Chainalysis, Silk Road, Welcome to Video, BTC-e).
gist: A true-crime account of investigators tracing cryptocurrency transactions to dismantle darknet markets and criminal networks. Reads as narrative journalism for general readers.

title: A Progressive's Case for Bitcoin
notes: Apr 2023; updated edition later.
gist: Argues for Bitcoin from a progressive viewpoint, covering its environmental impact, its effect on poor and marginalized communities, and its role as a check on too-big-to-fail banks. Needs no background knowledge.

title: Abundance Through Scarcity
gist: An illustrated, philosophical book arguing that scarcity is a basic feature of the universe and the route to abundance, critiquing modern work as a form of hidden servitude. For readers drawn to Bitcoin's philosophy.

title: Bitcoin is Better
gist: Argues that Bitcoin, as simple, transparent, energy-based money, can counter inflation and help build a better world, mixing personal stories, analysis and a call to action. For general readers.

title: Bitcoin vs Altcoins
gist: Compares Bitcoin with other cryptocurrencies, covering proof-of-work versus proof-of-stake, smart contracts, the Lightning Network, decentralization and network effects. Aimed at readers wanting a technical and economic comparison.

title: Bitcoin: A Game Theoretic Analysis
free_link_note: Book is a paid De Gruyter textbook (not open access). Author's GitHub has related Python simulations/problem solutions, no book text, no license.
evidence: micah541 is Micah Warren (his UOregon page links github.com/micah541/censorship); repo 'Game Theory and Probability for Bitcoin' holds mining/game-theory scripts and problem solutions matching the book's topics. Loosely companion, not declared as such.
gist: A mathematics textbook applying probability and game theory to Bitcoin's security, covering Nakamoto consensus, selfish mining, attack incentives and mining economics. Aimed at students and researchers.

title: Broken Money
subtitle: Why Our Financial System Is Failing Us and How We Can Make It Better
gist: Traces the history of money as technology, from shell money and gold to central banks and Bitcoin, and argues the current financial system is failing and could be improved. Suited to general readers.

title: Cryptosovereignty
gist: A collection of essays on Bitcoin, sovereignty and cryptography, approached through continental political philosophy. Suited to readers interested in philosophy of Bitcoin.

title: Decrypting Money
gist: An introduction to Bitcoin for general readers, covering blockchains, mining, private keys and the history of money from fiat to cryptocurrency, without technical jargon.

title: Die orange Pille
subtitle: Warum Bitcoin weit mehr als nur ein neues Geld ist
notes: Spiegel bestseller by a Die Zeit literary critic.
gist: A personal account by a German literary critic of his path into Bitcoin, explaining the technology and the case against central-bank money with humour. Written in German for newcomers; not an investment guide.

title: Fiat Ruins Everything
notes: Aug 2023. Critique of fiat money from a Bitcoin perspective.
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; Bitcoin Magazine Books catalog (bitcoinmagazine.com/bitcoin-magazine-books)
gist: Argues that debasement of money is the root of many social problems, from banking and real estate to education and art, and that Bitcoin can reverse them. Written for general readers.

title: Gradually, Then Suddenly
subtitle: A Framework for Understanding Bitcoin as Money
free_link_note: Free to read online at Satoshi Nakamoto Institute (publisher's library)
gist: Parker Lewis's essay series on Bitcoin and money, collected as a book that builds an intuitive framework for understanding Bitcoin as hard money. Aimed at non-technical readers.

title: Hidden Repression
subtitle: How the IMF and World Bank Sell Exploitation as Development
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; Bitcoin Magazine Books catalog (bitcoinmagazine.com/bitcoin-magazine-books)

title: History Echoes Bitcoin
gist: Examines Bitcoin's characteristics through historical examples, such as the Iroquois Confederacy and debates over communism and capitalism. For Bitcoin readers interested in history.

title: Mastering Bitcoin
subtitle: Programming the Open Blockchain (3rd Edition)
free_link_note: CC-BY-SA 4.0 (3rd ed.; 1st and 2nd editions also CC-BY-SA in same repo as release tags). Read chapters on GitHub; translations via bitcoinbook.info/Transifex
sources: Official repo github.com/bitcoinbook/bitcoinbook README (HTTP 200, license text checked)
notes: 1st ed. 2014 (subtitle 'Unlocking Digital Cryptocurrencies', Antonopoulos alone), 2nd ed. 2017, 3rd ed. Dec 2023 co-authored with David A. Harding. Translations: Spanish (community), Japanese (NTT出版, 『ビットコインとブロックチェーン』), many others.
gist: A technical reference on Bitcoin, covering keys, addresses, transactions, the peer-to-peer network, mining and security, plus Taproot and Lightning. The third edition was updated by David Harding; for developers and technical readers.

title: Number Go Up
subtitle: Inside Crypto's Wild Rise and Staggering Fall
notes: Mostly about FTX, Tether and the crypto bubble; Bitcoin is not the focus.
gist: A journalist's investigation of the crypto boom and bust, covering Sam Bankman-Fried and FTX, pig-butchering scams and the promoters behind crypto's rise. Critical of the industry; for general readers.

title: Proof of Money
gist: A Bitcoin primer treating it as an alternative monetary model rather than a trading vehicle, covering it as a bearer asset and store of value. Aimed at readers who know crypto basics.

title: Softwar
subtitle: A Novel Theory on Power Projection and the National Strategic Significance of Bitcoin
gist: Argues that Bitcoin's proof-of-work gives cyberspace a physical form of power projection and deterrence, with national-security implications. Expanded from an MIT thesis by a US Space Force officer.

title: The Bible and Bitcoin
gist: A Christian introduction to Bitcoin by a pastor, covering the biblical case for honest money, how Bitcoin works, and critiques of fiat money and fractional reserve banking. Aimed at Christian readers new to Bitcoin.

title: The Bitcoin Handbook
subtitle: Key Concepts in Economics, Technology & Psychology
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; Konsensus Network catalog (via litres.ru author page / konsensus.net search)
gist: A short, illustrated collection of frameworks, mental models and heuristics for understanding money and Bitcoin in the digital age. Aimed at general readers who want visual explanations of key concepts.

title: The Bitcoin-Dollar
notes: Aug 2023; listed as 'The Bitcoin-Dollar Book' on the catalogue page.
gist: Argues that money is technology for carrying trust across time and space, and that Bitcoin is the next step in money's evolution rather than a mere dollar replacement. Draws on economics and monetary history.

title: The Hidden Cost of Money
gist: A long, critical look at how money shapes social, economic and political life, arguing that many modern problems trace back to the monetary system and that Bitcoin offers a way out.

title: The Philosophy of Bitcoin
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; Bitcoin Magazine Books catalog (bitcoinmagazine.com/bitcoin-magazine-books)
gist: Translation of a Spanish work examining Bitcoin's nature and political consequences. Argues that money needs no state backing, that nation-states are not the only viable political form, and that Bitcoin makes property absolute.

title: Why Bitcoin?
sources: Goodreads list 'Bitcoin, Money & the Economy'; bitcoin-resources.com/books
gist: A collection of short essays explaining why Bitcoin exists, its global impact and personal significance. Written for newcomers and experienced users alike, with no economics or computing background needed.

title: Bitcoin Explained Like I'm 5
subtitle: A Simple Guide
gist: A short illustrated beginner's guide to Bitcoin using simple explanations and cartoon characters. It grew out of an internal training presentation at a Bitcoin exchange.

title: Bitcoin Prophecy
gist: Argues for Bitcoin as an alternative to broken monetary systems, using Argentina's history of inflation, devaluation and exchange controls as the case study. Written by a Bitcoin meetup organizer.

title: Hijacking Bitcoin
subtitle: The Hidden History of BTC
gist: A history of Bitcoin's development and the blocksize wars from Roger Ver's perspective, arguing that a small group of insiders changed the protocol after Satoshi left. For readers interested in the BTC versus BCH dispute.

title: I Am Not Your Bruh
notes: June 2024.

title: Intro to Bitcoin
subtitle: Hope for a Better World
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: A beginner-friendly primer covering Bitcoin basics, the Lightning Network, mining and energy, human rights and common myths. Written for people new to Bitcoin.

title: Introduction to Bitcoin
gist: A historical survey of the characteristics of money, arguing that Bitcoin shows the traits of sound money. Written by a Philippine law professor for general readers.

title: National Security in the Digital Age
sources: thingelstad.com Bitcoin Books list; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: A multi-author volume arguing that Bitcoin is a tool of modern statecraft, with essays on its implications for national security and great-power competition. Aimed at policy-minded readers.

title: Parallel
gist: Examines Bitcoin as a social and cultural movement rather than only a speculative asset, drawing comparisons with historical revolutions. Co-written with Knut Svanholm and Daniel Prince.

title: Pay Attention to Bitcoin
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)

title: Resistance Money
subtitle: A Philosophical Case for Bitcoin
notes: Routledge, June 2024. Academic philosophy authors.
sources: Routledge; resistance.money FAQ; Princeton book talk
lopp.net bitcoin books pages; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: An academic philosophical case that Bitcoin is a net good, examining its monetary policy, censorship resistance, privacy, inclusion and energy use, and testing the strongest objections. Written for readers from newcomers to skeptics.

title: Shells to Satoshi
gist: A history of money from ancient times to the digital age, tracing its evolution through historical and anthropological perspectives to the rise of Bitcoin.

title: The Atlas Maneuver
notes: Cotton Malone #18; Bitcoin is the plot driver.
gist: A Cotton Malone thriller in which a Swiss bank, the CIA and hidden wartime gold collide with a plot to weaponize bitcoin against the world's financial systems. Fiction for thriller readers.

title: The Big Bitcoin Book
gist: A visual history of Bitcoin's first fifteen years, aimed at general readers.

title: The Bitcoin Miners Almanac
notes: Bitcoin Magazine Books, June 2024.
gist: An introduction to Bitcoin mining covering how it works and the operational and business considerations, followed by interviews and case studies of different mining business models.

title: The Bitcoin Singularity
notes: Dystopian 2026 London; plot involves Satoshi's coins.
gist: A young-adult dystopian thriller set in London in 2026, in which a teenager and her AI companion try to protect coins vital to Bitcoin's stability from a villain seeking control. Fiction.

title: The Bushido of Bitcoin
gist: Presents ten virtues, such as courage, honor and self-control, as a code of character for people living on a Bitcoin standard, drawing on samurai ethics and Austrian economics.

title: The Conservative Case for Bitcoin
gist: Argues that Bitcoin's hard money supports traditional American conservative values, including family stability and protection from inflation. Written by a Bitcoin mining company researcher.

title: The Dao of Bitcoin
gist: Frames Bitcoin as energy money tied to human time and effort, using Daoist ideas about the Dao and qi, and explores decentralization and the orange-pill awakening.

title: The Genesis Book
subtitle: The Story of the People and Projects That Inspired Bitcoin
notes: Released 3 Jan 2024. Italian translation exists.
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; Bitcoin Magazine Books catalog (bitcoinmagazine.com/bitcoin-magazine-books)
gist: A history of the ideas and people behind Bitcoin before its launch, including the cypherpunks, David Chaum's ecash and Wei Dai's b-money. By a Bitcoin journalist.

title: The Nakamoto Consensus
gist: A Bitcoin thriller about the disappearance of Satoshi Nakamoto, in which a protagonist must protect Satoshi and defend Bitcoin from those trying to corrupt it. Fiction, with a Socratic dialogue element.

title: Twenty One Questions
gist: A beginner's guide to Bitcoin organized around 21 questions, written with an AI language model and contributions from several Bitcoin authors. Aimed at newcomers.

title: Walking Banks
gist: A murder-mystery thriller set in Beijing in which a U.S. Embassy official is killed, and a hidden bitcoin fortune and a central bank digital currency opponent figure in the case. Fiction.

title: Would Mao Hold Bitcoin?
notes: June 2024. Bitcoin and China.
sources: Bitcoin Magazine Books catalog (bitcoinmagazine.com/bitcoin-magazine-books); nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: Traces China's relationship with Bitcoin, from government bans to citizen adoption, and examines how the digital yuan and CBDCs interact with open-source freedom technology in techno-nationalist China.

title: Bitcoin Age
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: Examines humanity's search for ideal money, covering the dollar's rise, global banking and inflationary money creation, and presents Bitcoin as a store of value alternative to the credit-money system.

title: Bitcoin Is for Everyone
gist: Argues that rising costs of housing, tuition and groceries trace back to a broken monetary system, and presents Bitcoin as the fix. Written for general readers by a financial journalist and podcast host.

title: Bitcoin One Million
gist: Makes a math-and-logic case that Bitcoin is on a path to $1 million, comparing it with stocks, bonds, gold and real estate and discussing allocation with the Kelly Criterion.

title: Energy Use in Bitcoin Mining
subtitle: The Environmental Impact of Cryptocurrencies
gist: An academic assessment of Bitcoin mining's electricity use and environmental damages, including climate, air pollution, e-waste, water and land use, with a discussion of greener mining and policy obstacles.

title: Future Proof
gist: Links Bitcoin and longevity, presenting self-custody of both health and money as the core idea, with AI-driven health tools and Bitcoin as financial security. A self-published follow-up to the author's beginner primer.

title: Modern Chains
gist: A moral and philosophical critique of the modern monetary system as a mechanism of economic enslavement, targeting fractional reserve banking, debt-based money, inflation and usury, and proposing a monetary alternative.

title: Principles of Bitcoin
subtitle: Technology, Economics, Politics, and Philosophy
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: A first-principles examination of Bitcoin through technology, economics, politics and philosophy, by a former Goldman Sachs lawyer. Aimed at readers seeking a structured framework for analyzing Bitcoin.

title: Satoshi's Gift
gist: An introduction to Bitcoin's history, promise and power, covering monetary history and the forces behind its creation and arguing against debt, inflation and centralized control. A debut by a practicing attorney.

title: Self Bitcoinization
gist: A philosophical take on Bitcoin by an emergency physician, discussing its societal and individual impact and the implications of the current monetary system.

title: The Big Print
subtitle: What Happened to America and How Sound Money Will Fix It
gist: Examines how America's monetary system went astray and caused pain through inflation, then offers solutions based on sound money. Also gives investment guidance on protecting against inflation.

title: The Devil Takes Bitcoin
subtitle: Cryptocurrency Crimes and the Japanese Connection
notes: Scribe, Sept 2025 (AU), Oct 2025 (US). Mt. Gox-centred but covers wider Japanese crypto crime.
gist: A nonfiction account of cryptocurrency crime centered on the collapse of the Mt. Gox exchange in Tokyo, with the Silk Road marketplace and Japanese connections. Narrative reporting by the author of Tokyo Vice.

title: The Little Book of Bitcoin
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets)
gist: A Wiley guide for investors explaining Bitcoin, blockchain basics, Bitcoin as a store of value, and how institutions approach trading and holding it. Written by a hedge-fund manager for readers from newcomers to professionals, with a foreword by Michael Saylor.

title: The Mysterious Mr. Nakamoto
subtitle: A Fifteen-Year Quest to Unmask the Secret Genius Behind Crypto
gist: A journalist's account of his fifteen-year hunt for Bitcoin's creator, weighing suspects such as Hal Finney and Craig Wright and drawing on interviews, public records and stylometry. For general readers interested in Satoshi's identity and Bitcoin's cypherpunk roots.

title: The Satoshi Papers
notes: Edited volume (Smolenski is editor). Paperback Mar 2025, library edition May 2025.
gist: An edited volume of ten essays on how money and the state relate in a world with Bitcoin, framed by the Federalist and Anti-Federalist debates. Contributors include academics and policy writers; aimed at readers interested in Bitcoin policy and political theory.

title: Bitcoin l'eletto
notes: OM edizioni, 'I Saggi' series, 327 pp. Content not verified beyond listing.
gist: An Italian novel inspired by Bitcoin's birth and the figure of Satoshi Nakamoto, mixing real events with fiction to critique centralized finance and prompt questions about how money is controlled. For general Italian readers.

title: Crypto for Kids
subtitle: Discover Bitcoin and Blockchain the Fun Way
notes: Ages 9+. Title suggests general crypto content.
gist: A children's book following a group of young characters through story-driven adventures, puzzles and games that introduce Bitcoin, blockchain, wallets, mining, NFTs, smart contracts and DeFi. Aimed at ages 9 and up.

title: Defending Bitcoin
subtitle: Industrial-Grade Cybersecurity for the Monetary Grid
free_link_note: Complete book free to read in browser on author's official site (license not stated); print sold separately
sources: defendingbitcoin.com (200, 'The complete book, read in your browser for free'); subtitle per Bitcoin Infinity/BTC Prague bio
nakamotolibrary.org (via search snippets); Bitcoin Infinity Show
gist: Applies industrial control-system security standards (ISA/IEC 62443), defense-in-depth and threat modeling to Bitcoin, arguing it is critical monetary infrastructure. Aimed at bitcoiners and technical security professionals; foreword by Mikko Hyppönen.

title: Digital Real Estate
gist: A real estate developer's argument that Bitcoin is taking over the monetary premium real estate has long held as a store of value. Covers Bitcoin-backed mortgages, pricing property in bitcoin and treasury strategies for developers.

title: The Belief Machine
gist: Not a technical Bitcoin primer; it uses Bitcoin to examine how identity, belonging, status and inherited beliefs shape what feels true, and why facts rarely change minds. Touches on self-custody, volatility and patience.

title: The Bitcoin Mask
subtitle: Who Owned Satoshi
notes: Self-published financial thriller about the Satoshi myth.
gist: A 2026 financial thriller about Bitcoin, anonymity and market manipulation, following a Swiss-Italian economist and a young trader who loses family savings. It is less about who Satoshi is than who benefits from the mystery.

title: The Physics of Bitcoin
gist: Applies statistical physics and power-law analysis to Bitcoin's long-term growth and price, developing the author's Bitcoin Power Law model from first principles and fifteen years of data. For readers comfortable with quantitative arguments.

title: Unconfiscatable
gist: A 2026 debut thriller about a Chicago probate lawyer who inherits the keys to billions in Bitcoin and is pursued by a cartel, the FBI and a government operative. Fiction for general readers.

title: 21 Futures
subtitle: Tales from the Timechain
sources: Konsensus Network catalog (via litres.ru author page / konsensus.net search); Bitcoin Magazine review
gist: A Bitcoin fiction anthology of twenty-one short stories by twenty-one authors, exploring privacy, personal liberty and financial freedom through cypherpunk-style speculative fiction. Edited by Philip Charter and Niko Laamanen.

title: 21 Ways
subtitle: 21 Ways To Look At Bitcoin
free_link_note: Work in progress; published chapters free online, CC-BY-SA 4.0
gist: Gigi's follow-up to 21 Lessons, looking at Bitcoin from many angles using metaphors from biology, physics and engineering. Described as a work in progress, with some chapters already public.

title: B Is for Bitcoin
gist: A children's alphabet book that pairs each letter with a Bitcoin or crypto term, such as blockchain or consensus, with a short explanation and illustration. Also suited to adults wanting a basic introduction.

title: Bitcoin 2140 Genesis
subtitle: A Tale of Digital Gold and Human Freedom
gist: First novel in a six-book science fiction series imagining a world after fiat currencies collapse and incorruptible money reshapes civilization, featuring a Council of Satoshi. Fiction for readers who like Bitcoin-themed speculative stories.

title: Bitcoin a jiné kryptopeníze budoucnosti
subtitle: Historie, ekonomie a technologie kryptoměn
notes: Grada; editions confirmed 2018 and 2021 (3rd ext. ed.); Slovak translation 2024. First-edition year not confirmed. Covers other cryptocurrencies too but Bitcoin-centred.
gist: A Czech guide to the history, economics and technology of Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies, asking whether Bitcoin can work as digital money and whether it is a bubble. Written by two economists, with a beginner's guide included; the 2018 first edition was by Dominik Stroukal and Jan Skalicky.

title: Bitcoin Alpha v0.01
gist: A book presenting the original Bitcoin source code released by Satoshi Nakamoto in 2009, with color-coded and numbered lines for easy reference. For readers who want to read the first implementation directly.

title: Bitcoin Design Guide
free_link_note: Not a traditional book: a free, open-source online design reference for bitcoin applications
notes: Online design reference, not a book.
gist: A free, open-source guide for designers and developers building non-custodial Bitcoin products, with design principles, reference wallet designs, a glossary and a technology primer. Version 2 focuses on Lightning wallets.

title: Bitcoin Diploma
subtitle: Mi Primer Bitcoin / My First Bitcoin curriculum
free_link_note: Open-source curriculum book (student guide) on official GitHub, ~23 languages; earlier editions CC-BY-SA, current repo license not stated
sources: Official MyFirstBitcoin GitHub org (200). Old Bitcoin-Diploma-2025 repo now 404
gist: A free, open-source student workbook for a 10-week Bitcoin course, covering the history of money, problems with fiat, the Lightning Network and how Bitcoin works technically. Created for school education, with many translations.

title: Bitcoin en Blockchain
notes: By Dutch tech journalist (BNR). ~170 pp. Year not confirmed; title also covers blockchain but is Bitcoin-led.
gist: A Dutch practical guide by a tech journalist to buying, holding and safely keeping bitcoin, plus the theory and history of Bitcoin and blockchain, largely in question-and-answer form. Light on monetary theory.

title: Bitcoin for Kiddos
gist: A children's picture book telling the story of Bitcoin, written and illustrated by a couple to start playful conversations with kids about money. Aimed at young children and their parents.

title: Bitcoin Mining Economics
gist: A Braiins book on mining as a business, covering energy markets, intermittent power, stranded natural gas, cooling options, debt financing and future revenue. Written mainly by Daniel Frumkin, with contributors including Karim Helmy.

title: Bitcoin Programming
subtitle: A textbook
free_link_note: free PDF, author's GitHub

title: Bitcoin: A Work in Progress
free_link_note: CC-BY-SA 4.0 (LICENSE.md, Copyright Sjors Provoost), full manuscript in Markdown/Pandoc; paperback PDFs attached to releases (e.g. v1.0.5: https://github.com/Sjors/nado-book/releases/tag/v1.0.5)
evidence: Repo owned by author's GitHub account Sjors; description 'Bitcoin: A Work in Progress (book source code)', homepage btcwip.com (official book site)
gist: A Bitcoin Core contributor's account of recent Bitcoin developments, including Taproot, protecting open source code from bugs and malware, and blockchain growth, with links to matching Bitcoin, Explained podcast episodes. For readers wanting a technical but accessible overview.

title: Bitcoin: Odluka peněz od státu
notes: English edition 'Bitcoin: Separation of Money and State' (Braiins, 2023, 119 pp). Czech original year not confirmed.
gist: A Czech book on separating money from the state, covering the Austrian school of economics, time preference, monetary history, and why the author thinks only Bitcoin can succeed as sound money.

title: Energy, the Flip Side of Money
sources: Konsensus Network catalog (via litres.ru author page / konsensus.net search)
gist: An engineer's essay on how energy and information underpin society and money, restating the principles of thermodynamics and applying them to everyday life and economics. Published by Konsensus Network; translated from the French original.

title: Goodnight Bitcoin
gist: A children's bedtime book telling the story of Bitcoin's origins, from Satoshi Nakamoto's creation to the first transaction sent to Hal Finney, with early skepticism and how the network keeps running. Aimed at young children and their parents.

title: If You Give a Monster a Bitcoin
Kicking the Hornet's Nest
subtitle: The Complete Writings, Emails, and Forum Posts of Satoshi Nakamoto
free_link_note: GPL-3.0 repo with full compilation PDF (Kicking_the_Hornets_Nest-010319.pdf, 2019 edition) of Satoshi's writings; newer editions (incl. COPA emails) are distributed free by the compiler via links in his hive.blog post https://hive.blog/@crrdlx/satoshi
evidence: Repo owned by crrdlx, who is the compiler of the collection (his hive.blog post lists the official free PDF/text copies and the Lulu print edition). Underlying texts are Satoshi's public writings. Repo is from 2020 so it holds an older edition.
gist: A chronological compilation of Satoshi Nakamoto's public writings: emails, forum posts and mailing-list messages, with minimal editorial commentary. Edited by Mill Hill Books; later editions add emails released in the COPA trial.

title: L'uomo più ricco del mondo
notes: Investigation into the identity of Satoshi Nakamoto. Year not confirmed.
gist: An Italian investigative account of who Satoshi Nakamoto might be, reviewing suspects such as Hal Finney, Nick Szabo and Gavin Andresen before concluding that the identity matters less than the idea. Published by Rizzoli in 2022.

title: Onboarding to Bitcoin Core
subtitle: The missing onboarding guide to Bitcoin Core
free_link_note: Free online guide/book (Chaincode Labs); source on GitHub
gist: An open onboarding guide for people who want to contribute to Bitcoin Core, covering getting started, the software's workflow and architecture. Maintained as a GitHub repository by Will Clark with Chaincode Labs.

title: Orange Pilled
subtitle: A Brief Introduction to Bitcoin

title: Praxeology
subtitle: The Invisible Hand That Feeds Bitcoin
sources: lopp.net bitcoin books pages; Konsensus Network catalog (via litres.ru author page / konsensus.net search)
gist: An introduction to praxeology, the study of human action, which analyses society starting from individual choices and uses a Robinson Crusoe story to show how people value goods and time. Written for general readers; subtitled The Invisible Hand That Feeds You.

title: Programming the Blockchain in C#
free_link_note: Free open-source book (NBitcoin) on GitBook; source on GitHub; Indonesian/Japanese/Korean translations
sources: Official repo README links to GitBook (200)
gist: A free, Creative Commons guide to Bitcoin programming with the NBitcoin .NET library, covering transactions, key generation, multisig, HD wallets, colored coins and building a wallet. For C# developers.

title: The Praxeology of Privacy
free_link_note: free ebook from publisher (Konsensus)
gist: Combines Austrian economics with cypherpunk cryptography to argue that privacy is needed for purposeful action, covering financial surveillance, CBDCs, the cryptographic stack and Bitcoin privacy tools such as CoinJoin and Lightning. Subtitled Economic Logic in Cypherpunk Implementation.

title: The UnCommunist Manifesto
sources: Goodreads list 'Bitcoin, Money & the Economy'; Konsensus Network catalog (via litres.ru author page / konsensus.net search)
gist: A rewrite of Marx and Engels' manifesto, in similar length and structure, framing the real conflict as individual sovereignty and responsibility versus collectivist coercion. For readers interested in the political philosophy around Bitcoin.
